ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a gray orthogonal polygon garden, with a shape similar to a notched stair-step shape or “C” shape. All sides are horizontal or vertical. The figure marks the length of the entire vertical side on the left as 3, the length of the topmost horizontal side as 5, and the length of a horizontal side near the lower middle as 4. Reasoning: Walking once around this closed orthogonal polygon, the total length of all horizontal sides going right must equal the total length of all horizontal sides going left. The two lengths in the figure that can serve as horizontal movement to the right are respectively 5 and 4, so the total horizontal length to the right is 5+4=9, therefore the total length of all horizontal sides is 2×9=18. The vertical direction is the same; in a closed figure, the total length of vertical sides going down equals the total length of vertical sides going up. The entire vertical side on the left is 3, so the stepped vertical sides on the other side also total 3, and the total length of all vertical sides is 2×3=6. Therefore the perimeter is 18+6=24.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as an orthogonal polygon: the top horizontal side is 5, the lower interior-to-right horizontal side is 4, and the full left vertical side is 3. Traverse the perimeter. Because the path closes, the total length of all rightward horizontal moves equals the total length of all leftward horizontal moves. The two known rightward horizontal moves are 5 and 4, so all horizontal boundary length is 2(5+4)=18. Similarly, the total downward vertical boundary length on the stepped right/interior side must equal the single upward/left-side height 3, so all vertical boundary length is 2·3=6. Add horizontal and vertical contributions: 18+6=24.

method.method_draft: Assign variables to the unknown step lengths visible in the diagram. Let x be the horizontal distance from the left side to the inner vertical notch. Then the unknown upper inward horizontal segment has length 5−x, while the unknown bottom horizontal side has length x+4 because the labeled lower horizontal segment from the notch to the right edge is 4. Their sum is therefore (5−x)+(x+4)=9. Let the three unlabeled vertical segments on the right/interior side be a, b, and c; together they descend from the top level to the bottom level, so a+b+c=3, matching the labeled left side height. Now add all perimeter pieces: known horizontals 5+4, unknown horizontals 9, left vertical 3, and other verticals 3, giving 24.

把所有边长相加：已知水平边为 5 + 4 = 9，未知水平边之和为 9，左侧竖边为 3，其余竖边之和为 3。所以周长为 9 + 9 + 3 + 3 = 24。
